_disclaimer: Synthetic/illustrative FIXTURE data for the ayurveda-oncology-support proposal's schema and validator. Evidence summaries are drawn from the study descriptions supplied for this proposal and have NOT been re-verified against full-text primary sources in this pass (see verification_status on each cited source in source_registry.json). Do not treat any card here as clinically approved or patient-visible. No card may ever gain a recommended_dose field or an autonomous 'recommended' state -- both are rejected by scripts/validate_ayurveda_proposal.py.

cards.cancer_context: Primary or secondary malignant brain tumors during radiotherapy
cards.population: Adults with primary or secondary brain tumors receiving RT

herb.preparation: standardized gum-resin extract (not culinary, not tea)

cards.supportive_care_purpose: Possible reduction of radiotherapy-associated cerebral edema -- a supportive-care endpoint, not a tumor-directed or steroid-replacement claim

evidence.summary: One small randomized, double-blind pilot trial reported reduced RT-associated cerebral edema versus placebo.

cards.limitations: Single small pilot; not independently replicated; supportive imaging/edema endpoint only, not survival or tumor response.

known_concerns: potential interaction with anti-edema/steroid regimens not to be assumed absent clinician review

cards.population: Adults with breast cancer receiving chemotherapy
cards.supportive_care_purpose: Possible improvement in cancer-related fatigue and quality of life during chemotherapy

evidence.summary: Open-label, nonrandomized comparative study; no proven tumor-control or survival benefit.

cards.limitations: No randomization or blinding; high risk of bias; fatigue is subjective and susceptible to placebo/expectation effects.

never_imply: chemotherapy replacement or dose reduction rationale
known_concerns: Withania is contraindicated or requires caution in some thyroid, sedative, and immunosuppressant contexts -- not assessed here

cards.treatment_context: Chemotherapy with standard antiemetic background varying by trial

herb.preparation: ginger / standardized 6-gingerol preparations (not equivalent to raw culinary ginger)

cards.supportive_care_purpose: Adjunct to -- never a substitute for -- prescribed antiemetics for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting

evidence.summary: Mixed: at least one trial reports benefit for CINV; a separate trial in an AC breast-chemotherapy regimen with ondansetron/dexamethasone found no benefit (see card-ginger-ac-null for that specific context, kept separate rather than averaged away).

cards.limitations: Preparation, dose standardization, chemotherapy regimen, and background antiemetic regimen all differ between trials and are not interchangeable.

red_flags_requiring_escalation: persistent vomiting unable to keep fluids down

cards.treatment_context: AC chemotherapy with ondansetron and dexamethasone antiemetic background
cards.population: Adults with breast cancer on AC with standard antiemetic prophylaxis
cards.supportive_care_purpose: Investigated as adjunct for nausea/vomiting; this specific trial found no added benefit

evidence.summary: Randomized trial found no significant benefit of ginger capsules over placebo when added to ondansetron/dexamethasone in this regimen.

cards.limitations: Null result specific to this regimen and antiemetic background; must not be silently merged into the general ginger/CINV card's evidence average.

never_imply: ginger is proven ineffective for CINV in all regimens (overgeneralization)
red_flags_requiring_escalation: persistent vomiting unable to keep fluids down

herb.preparation: Multi-component whole-systems Ayurveda nutrition/lifestyle program (not a single herb)

cards.supportive_care_purpose: Feasibility and acceptability of a structured lifestyle program; effect on self-reported symptoms and quality of life

evidence.summary: Single-arm feasibility study; no recurrence-prevention or disease-efficacy claim is supported.

cards.limitations: No control group; feasibility/acceptability endpoints only; cannot support any claim about cancer recurrence, progression, or survival.

known_concerns: program components (diet, herbs, routine) were not individually isolated for safety analysis
red_flags_requiring_escalation: any component conflicting with current oncology follow-up care

cards.general_education_scope: feasibility and patient experience only, not efficacy

cards.treatment_context: Proposed as adjunct across various treatment contexts in the source literature

herb.preparation: turmeric / curcumin-containing products (culinary spice, extract, and isolated curcumin are NOT equivalent and must not be conflated)

cards.supportive_care_purpose: Proposed anti-inflammatory/adjunct role; no cancer-treatment claim is supported

evidence.summary: Per current NCI PDQ conclusion, evidence is insufficient to support curcumin as a cancer treatment; bioavailability and formulation vary widely between products.

cards.limitations: Formulation heterogeneity (culinary vs. extract vs. isolated curcumin vs. bioavailability-enhanced products) makes pooling across studies unreliable.

known_concerns: possible interaction with anticoagulants and some chemotherapy agents
high-dose extract not equivalent to dietary turmeric

cards.cancer_context: Leukemia, multiple myeloma, male breast cancer, Bartholin gland cancer
cards.treatment_context: Marketed as standalone or adjunct 'natural treatment'
cards.population: As marketed to the general public
cards.supportive_care_purpose: None established -- registered here only to record that it was reviewed and blocked, not to imply a purpose

evidence.summary: Sourced entirely from commercial marketing pages selling herb packs; no independent human clinical evidence was supplied or located.

cards.limitations: Commercial pages do not by themselves establish efficacy or safety regardless of testimonial content or clinic affiliation.

known_concerns: proprietary multi-herb blends make ingredient-level safety and interaction review impossible without full disclosure
red_flags_requiring_escalation: patient already purchased or is taking one of these packs -- refer to treating oncology team
